claims.text: Ion irradiation can introduce a controlled amount of atomic-scale disorder into as-deposited FeMnNiGeSi-type nanoscale films or nanoribbons.
Ion-irradiation-induced atomic-scale disorder will enhance the magnetocaloric response relative to the unirradiated as-deposited baseline.
Ion-irradiation-induced atomic-scale disorder will reduce hysteresis relative to the unirradiated as-deposited baseline.
Atomic-scale disorder is the structural mediator governing the predicted changes in magnetocaloric response and hysteresis.
The proposed enhancement and hysteresis reduction are applicable over 100-300 K, applied fields of 0-1 T, and cycle frequencies of 1-10 Hz.
The relevant baseline is the same as-deposited FeMnNiGeSi-type nanoscale film or patterned nanoribbon without ion irradiation.
The relationship between atomic-scale disorder and magnetocaloric response is not well understood.
Failure to observe a significant change in either magnetocaloric response or hysteresis after irradiation would falsify the hypothesis.
